title: SandboxAQ Expands Switch AI with Trust and ROI Tools | SandboxAQ
content: New Switch capabilities build on its data sovereignty foundation and give companies a vendor-neutral way to measure and improve AI agents' cost and ROI, while managing risk PALO ALTO, Calif., Oct. 19, 2026 -- SandboxAQ today announced an expansion of its Switch AI offering, giving companies greater choice and control as they adopt and scale AI agents. Building on its open-source Switch Rooms offering, which brings people and AI agents together with shared, company-controlled context, SandboxAQ is introducing Switch Trust and Switch ROI to help organizations evaluate agent risk, measure business value, and optimize performance across the agents, models, and providers they choose. SandboxAQ launched Switch in August 2026 as a Commons Clause Apache 2.0 open-source offering built around the premise that companies should have the freedom to choose and change their AI agents, models, and providers without losing control of their context. Switch Rooms brings people and agents together across Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord and other workplace tools, enabling teams to work with the agents they choose while retaining ownership of their shared context, history, and knowledge. As AI technology evolves, organizations can adopt new agents and models without starting over or becoming dependent on a single provider. The first generation of enterprise AI largely measured adoption through seats, usage and token consumption. AI agents represent a fundamental shift: they can make decisions, take actions and work alongside people, creating a new set of expectations for oversight and accountability. Mount Sinai West's MSW Lab is already working with Switch Trust to build G Board, a framework that enables physicians to create clinical applications using AI agents. "In the MSW Lab, physicians build real healthcare software with AI agents, so we have to prove those agents behave safely," said Dr. Jeffrey Bander, Chief of Cardiology at Mount Sinai West and Associate Professor of Cardiology and Artificial Intelligence at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. "Switch AI gives us a way to build that trust into how we work, so our physicians can focus on solving clinical problems without having to become AI security experts. The new products extend that foundation with the controls enterprises need to move agents from experimentation into everyday work. Switch Trust: Make every agent safe to put on real work by finding, testing, and guarding every agent your company runs. It works in four steps: Switch ROI: Shows what every agent costs and delivers, with specific recommendations to lower cost and improve performance. It offers the following key features: The Switch platform brings these capabilities together to address a growing problem for enterprises: AI agents are multiplying faster than companies can determine whether they are safe, effective or worth the investment. Gartner predicts that more than 40 percent of agentic AI projects will be canceled by the end of 2027, while only 7 percent of leaders say they have established a return on their AI investments. "More agents doesn't automatically mean more value. We've seen this across many users: in cases where we thought agents could help avoid a net-new hire, the AI spend quickly became more expensive than hiring a full-time person," said Mohammed Aboul-Magd, GM of Switch AI at SandboxAQ. "That's why ROI can't just mean 'we adopted AI.' You need to know what every agent costs, what it delivers and how to make it better over time. That's the problem Switch ROI is built to solve." "We're entering a world where companies will have hundreds, potentially thousands, of AI agents working alongside their employees. But you wouldn't hire a thousand people without knowing their qualifications, what they'll cost or whether they're delivering results," said Jack Hidary, CEO of SandboxAQ. "The same discipline needs to apply to AI agents. And as the technology advances, companies must be able to switch to better agents and models without losing the knowledge they've built. The intelligence belongs inside the company, not the AI provider. To learn more about Switch AI and explore its offerings, visit switchagents.ai .
